# Condenser water heat rejection replacement — Papago Federal Center, Phoenix, Arizona, 95 % construction documents

You are the mechanical engineer of record's plant designer on a GSA campus in Phoenix, Arizona. The
project document library for this task is the directory tree around this file: `standards/` and
`water/` (the public criteria documents, regulations and technical references the project adopts, PDF),
`economics/` (the federal life-cycle costing data release with its readme, and the text of a supplement
edition, XLSX, TXT and PDF), `climate/` (station climatic records and their dataset documentation, CSV and
PDF), `vendor_data/` (reviewed submittals for the cooling tower cells, their fans and motors, the procured
chillers and the drift eliminators, budgetary pricing, plus the performance data sets and the reference
implementation source the project adopts as its simulation basis), `drawings/` (roof mechanical, roof
framing and electrical one-line sheets in DXF, plan units are feet), `schedules/` (chiller, load-profile and
panel schedules, XLSX), `specs/` (the project design-criteria memorandum DC-02, the life-cycle cost
analysis criteria EC-01, the cooling tower specification section and a specification excerpt, DOCX),
`site/` (the purveyor's reclaimed-water allocation correspondence, the electric utility's rate confirmation
and the water treatment programme memorandum, DOCX) and `correspondence/` (RFI responses). Not every document is
relevant, and the information you need is spread across them: **read the design-criteria memorandum DC-02
first and let it tell you which documents govern what, and which are retained for reference only.**

## Situation

Three condenser water heat rejection plants are being replaced, one on each of three roofs: the
Courthouse Central Utility Plant (CUP), the Data Annex (ANNEX) and the Laboratory Wing (LAB). The
chillers are already procured and their condenser-side limits are fixed. The condenser water pumps are
dedicated to the chillers and their hydraulic circuits are fixed. The electrical distribution is
existing: each plant connects to a motor control centre with a fixed spare capacity and no service
upgrade is in the scope. Makeup water is reclaimed water under a firm allocation from the municipal
purveyor, and blowdown is discharged to the sanitary sewer under a daily limit. Each roof offers a fixed
equipment zone, fixed outdoor air intake positions and roof framing with stated allowable superimposed
loads, and one revision of the roof mechanical sheet in the library is superseded.

Nothing about the cooling tower plants themselves has been selected: not the cell model, not the number
of cells, not the design condenser water flow, not the condenser water supply temperature or the way it
is reset, not the cycles of concentration the water is controlled to, not the drift eliminator, the
casing material, the fan motor or where the cells stand on the roof. All of that is yours.

This is a federal building: the owner selects the tower plant of each roof under the federal life-cycle
cost rules, and the criteria require each plant to be designed for the **highest life-cycle net savings**
relative to the basic design that the life-cycle cost analysis criteria define, consistent with every
requirement the project documents place on the plant. That is not necessarily the design with the lowest
energy or the lowest first cost; the analysis decides.

## Deliverable

Produce `output/submission.zip` containing, for **each** of the three plants P in {CUP, ANNEX, LAB}:

1. `CT_SCHEDULE_P.dxf` — the cooling tower schedule sheet and roof layout for that plant, with the
   layers, tags, schedule keys and title block the design-criteria memorandum prescribes, in the plan
   coordinates of the roof mechanical sheet: one schedule row per cell and one set of plant rows, and one
   closed rectangular outline per cell showing where its support frame stands on the roof.
2. `CT_CALC_P.xlsx` — the calculation workbook with the five sheets the memorandum's appendix lays out:
   the design point, the off-design scenario table (one row per scenario bin, **at least 40 rows**, **covering the whole year**, every
   required column populated with a number), the water balance, the energy roll-up and the life-cycle cost
   analysis.

plus, once for the package:

3. `constraint_register.csv` — columns `id, document, clause, requirement, value, items_bound`: every
   requirement you applied, each with the document and the clause, table or figure it comes from, the
   value you used and what it binds (cells, plant, package). Cite the real project documents and clauses,
   not this brief. The register is scored on recall of the requirements the grader checks (**at least
   70 % of the hard requirements must be present**, matched on document + clause) and on the absence of
   rows that cite a superseded, cancelled or non-adopted document as their authority; the `value` column
   is a record for the reviewer and is not itself scored.
   Extra correct rows are neutral, and **a hard requirement missing from the register makes every family
   it governs count as not passed**, on every plant. Rows whose **document** cell cites a superseded or
   cancelled document as their authority count against you: **a single such row fails the register
   family**. Recording that a document is superseded or cancelled while naming the one that governs is
   not such a row, and neither is citing a standard that an adopted document itself brings in.
4. `design_basis.md` — a short design basis: the governing documents, how you resolved every conflict you
   found in the library, the method you used for each part of the calculation, the governing constraint
   per plant stated in the form the design-criteria memorandum prescribes, and the margins and judgement
   calls you made.

## Deliverable schema — stated here in full

The **format** below is a contract, not part of the problem: the values are yours, the schema is given.
DC-02 Appendix A repeats it. The grader matches layer names, tags, keys, sheet names and column headers
**case-insensitively and separator-insensitively** (`-`, `_` and spaces are equivalent, and a unit in
brackets after a header is ignored), tag numbering may be zero-padded (`CT-1`, `CT-01`, `CT1` are the same
cell), and a documented list of common synonyms for each name is accepted. Numbers may carry thousands
separators and a trailing unit; they must not be text. Only the cell count, the cell model, the total
condenser water flow, the two setpoint numbers and the cycles of concentration are indispensable — a
missing or unreadable value anywhere else costs the one family that uses it, not the whole plant.

### `CT_SCHEDULE_P.dxf`

Plan units feet, in the coordinates of the roof mechanical sheet. Three layers are read:

* **`M-CTWR-SCHD`** — one TEXT or MTEXT entity per scheduled field, written `<TAG> <KEY> <VALUE>`.
  `<TAG>` is `CT-1` … `CT-n` for the cell rows (one set of rows per installed cell, all identical) and
  `PLANT` for the plant rows.

  | cell row key | meaning | unit |
  |---|---|---|
  | `MODEL` | the cell model designation from the tower submittal | — |
  | `GPM` | design circulating water flow through that cell | gpm |
  | `FANHP` | fan motor nameplate rating | hp |
  | `MOTOREFF` | motor nominal full-load efficiency | percent |
  | `MOTORPOLES` | motor pole count | — |
  | `MOTORENCL` | motor enclosure designation | — |
  | `ELIMINATOR` | drift eliminator class code from the submittal | — |
  | `DRIFT` | certified drift rate of that eliminator | percent of design water flow |
  | `MATERIAL` | casing / basin material option code from the submittal | — |
  | `OPWEIGHT` | operating weight of one cell | lb |
  | `SOUNDLW` | A-weighted sound power level of one cell at full fan speed | dB |

  | plant row key | meaning | unit |
  |---|---|---|
  | `CELLS` | number of cells installed | — |
  | `GPMTOTAL` | design condenser water flow with every chiller running | gpm |
  | `WBDESIGN` | the outdoor wet-bulb temperature the plant is sized at | deg F |
  | `CWSDESIGN` | scheduled condenser water supply temperature at the design point | deg F |
  | `RANGEDESIGN` | design range | deg F |
  | `APPROACHDESIGN` | design approach | deg F |
  | `CWSMIN` | supply temperature floor of the reset schedule | deg F |
  | `CWSOFFSET` | offset above the outdoor wet bulb in the reset schedule | deg F |
  | `COC` | cycles of concentration the water is controlled to | — |
  | `BASINCLR` | clear dimension from the top of the roof to the underside of the basin | ft |
  | `EVAPMETHOD` | which evaporation formulation the package used — **`SATURATED-EXIT` or `LOSS-FACTOR`** | — |
  | `BASINHEATER` | basin heater and heat-traced makeup provided — **`YES` or `NO`** | — |
  | `BLOWDOWNCTRL` | automatic blowdown and chemical feed provided — **`YES` or `NO`** | — |
  | `EQUALIZING` | equalising lines and automatic isolation provided — **`YES` or `NO`** | — |

* **`M-CTWR-PLAN`** — one closed LWPOLYLINE per installed cell, the rectangular plan outline of that
  cell's support frame, **in the plan coordinates of the roof mechanical sheet**, which draws the three
  plants on one sheet, each on its own origin. One per cell, no more, no fewer.
* **`G-TBLK`** — the title block, which must carry a revision.

### `CT_CALC_P.xlsx`

Five sheets. `DesignPoint`, `WaterBalance`, `Energy` and `LifeCycleCost` are two-column key/value sheets,
the key in column A and a **number** (or, where stated, one of the listed tokens) in column B. `OffDesign`
is a table with a header row and one row per scenario bin.

| sheet | required keys / columns (units in the name) |
|---|---|
| `DesignPoint` | `DesignWetBulb_F`, `DesignLoad_tons`, `HeatRejection_BTUH`, `CWFlow_gpm`, `Range_F`, `Approach_F`, `CWS_F`, `CWR_F`, `WaterFlowRatio`, `CellsInService`, `RedundancyWetBulb_F`, `RedundancyCapacity_tons`, `DryBulb996_F` |
| `OffDesign` | `WetBulb_F`, `DryBulb_F`, `Hours`, `Load_tons`, `ChillersOn`, `CellsOn`, `CWFlow_gpm`, `AirFlowRatio`, `FanPLR`, `Range_F`, `CWS_F`, `CWR_F`, `ChillerkW`, `FankW`, `PumpkW`, `TotalkW`, `Makeup_gpm` — at least 40 rows, every one of these columns populated with a number, and the `Hours` column summing to the year the criteria memorandum scales the scenario bins to |
| `WaterBalance` | `EvaporationMethod` (**`saturated-exit` or `loss-factor`**, and it must agree with `EVAPMETHOD` on the schedule), `AnnualEvaporation_kgal`, `AnnualDrift_kgal`, `AnnualBlowdown_kgal`, `AnnualMakeup_kgal`, `PeakDayMakeup_gal`, `CyclesOfConcentration`, `MaxAllowableCOC`, `ScalingIndexAtCWR` |
| `Energy` | `AnnualChillerEnergy_kWh`, `AnnualFanEnergy_kWh`, `AnnualPumpEnergy_kWh`, `AnnualPlantEnergy_kWh`, `PeakCoincidentDemand_kW`, `MCCSpareCapacity_kW` |
| `LifeCycleCost` | `DiscountRate`, `StudyPeriod_yr`, `ConstructionPeriod_yr`, `UPVStarElectricity`, `UPVStarWater`, `UPVNonFuel`, `Investment_USD`, `AnnualEnergyCost_USD`, `AnnualWaterCost_USD`, `AnnualOMCost_USD`, `PVEnergy_USD`, `PVWater_USD`, `PVOM_USD`, `PVReplacement_USD`, `PVSalvage_USD`, `LCC_USD`, `BasicDesignLCC_USD`, `NetSavings_USD` — the life-cycle cost analysis of the design as scheduled, as DC-02 Appendix A.2 defines each key |

Three definitions that the schema fixes, so that nobody has to guess them:

* **`PeakCoincidentDemand_kW`** is the largest total electrical demand of the chillers, the tower fans
  and the condenser water pumps operating together, **taken over the scenario bins and over nothing
  else**. It is a maximum over those bins, not a design-day figure: the design point is a sizing
  condition, not a scenario bin, and does not enter it. This is also the quantity the motor control
  centre's spare capacity limits.
* **`DesignPoint` reports what the selected equipment achieves** at the design point — the range,
  approach, supply and return temperatures and water flow rate ratio that follow from the model, cell
  count and flow you scheduled — **not the scheduled target**. A conservative schedule is good
  engineering: the DXF carries the number you commit to, this sheet carries the number the cells
  actually make.
* **`GPM` on a cell row** is `GPMTOTAL ÷ CELLS`, the flow through one cell with every installed cell in
  service. Where the staging rule leaves a cell out of service at some operating point, the scheduled
  figure does not change; the flow actually in each cell at each scenario belongs in `OffDesign`.

Extra sheets, extra keys and extra columns are ignored, never penalised.

### `design_basis.md`

Free prose, with one line per plant in exactly this form:

```
GOVERNING CONSTRAINT <plant>: <name> (relative margin <value>)
```

where `<plant>` is `CUP`, `ANNEX` or `LAB` and `<name>` is **exactly one** of the six the design-criteria
memorandum defines: `water allocation`, `electrical capacity`, `roof area`, `structural capacity`,
`condenser flow limit`, `tower capability`. The memorandum gives the margin definition for each. A line
naming two of them does not count. The stated margin is accepted when it is consistent, within 0.004,
with the margin computed from the quantities your own workbook reports (peak coincident demand, annual
makeup, design supply temperature), provided each of those is within the tolerance the workbook checks
apply to it — 10 % for peak demand and annual makeup, the larger of 0.8 °F and 10 % of the approach for
the supply temperature; a reported quantity outside its tolerance is replaced by the recomputed value.
The name is accepted when it is the smallest margin so computed, ties within 0.004.

It must also carry one line for each of the three documented conflicts the design-criteria memorandum
lists, in exactly this form:

```
CONFLICT <n>: ADOPTED <document> <clause> | SET ASIDE <document> <clause>
```

where `<n>` is `1`, `2` or `3` in the order the memorandum lists them, `<document>` is the designation a
document gives itself and `<clause>` is the paragraph, table or revision within it. Both sides must be
named. The memorandum says which three conflicts these are and where the subject matter is allocated;
deciding which side governs is yours.

## What is graded

The grader recomputes each plant from the design on your DXF with the project's own simulation basis —
the performance data sets and the reference implementation the criteria memorandum adopts — over
scenario bins built from the station record, and checks your workbook against that recomputation. Per
plant it scores 28 constraint families drawn from the documents: the life-cycle net savings the criteria
require, the design outdoor condition, tower
capability at the design point, the validity envelope of the performance model, the condenser and cell
flow limits, redundancy, the cycles of concentration the water chemistry allows, the reclaimed water
allocation, the electrical spare capacity, fan power and speed, siting and clearances, roof framing
capacity, the condenser water temperature limits of the machines, motor efficiency, cell matching, and then
the reporting families — the design point report, the water balance, drift, materials,
blowdown controls, the freeze determination, sound, deliverable format, the register, the design
basis, the economic basis of the life-cycle cost analysis and the life-cycle cost report. The cycles of
concentration may not exceed the allowable cycles the treatment programme gives at the design condenser
water return temperature; a value written to two decimals is accepted up to 0.01 above it (rounding), and
anything beyond that fails.

The reporting families compare what your workbook reports with the grader's recomputation of your own
design, with these tolerances: annual plant energy, peak coincident demand, annual makeup and the other
water-balance quantities within 10 % (annual drift within 30 % or 1,000 gallons, whichever is larger); heat rejection and range within 5 %; design load and condenser
water flow within 1 %; the MCC spare capacity within 1 %; the design wet bulb within 0.3 °F and the
redundancy wet bulb and 99.6 % dry bulb within 1 °F; cells in service exact; the design supply
temperature and approach anywhere between what the selected cells achieve and the conservative
scheduled value, with the larger of 0.8 °F and 10 % either side; water flow rate ratio within 0.03;
redundancy capacity within 6 % (at least 20 tons); the three component energies summing to the plant
energy within 2 %; the off-design table's hours summing to the year within 2 %; and, in the off-design
table's rows for the three scenario bins with the most hours (located by their bin mid-points), the total
kW within 10 % and the supply temperature within the larger of 0.8 °F and 10 % of that bin's approach.
On the `LifeCycleCost` sheet: the discount rate within 0.0001 (a fraction, or a percentage), the two
periods exact, the electricity and non-fuel factors within 0.5 % and the water factor within 1 %; the
investment within 1 %; the annual costs and the energy, water and operation-and-maintenance present
values within 10 %; the replacement and salvage present values within 5 % or $5,000, whichever is larger;
the life-cycle cost within 5 %, the basic design's within 3 %, and the net savings within the larger of
25 % of the net savings and 1 % of the basic design's life-cycle cost; the life-cycle cost must be the
investment plus the present values less the salvage, and the net savings the basic design's life-cycle
cost less it, each within 1 %.

Hard families discount the objective. The grader prices your design itself, exactly as the life-cycle cost
analysis criteria direct, from its own recomputation of the plant, and the objective credit is
O = NS / NS* clipped to [0, 1], where NS is the net savings of your design against the basic design of the
same plant and NS* is the net savings of the best design of that plant known to the grader that meets every
requirement of the project documents; a design that matches or beats it earns the full objective credit. A
design with no net savings earns no objective credit. Because the criteria require the highest net savings,
the net savings are also a hard family: a plant whose NS falls more than 1 % short of NS* fails it. Score
per plant = 0.4·p² + 0.6·h⁴·O, where p is the fraction of the 28 families that count and h the fraction of
the 15 hard families that count; a family counts when the plant passes it and the register carries the hard
requirements that govern it. A hard failure does not withhold the objective credit; it discounts it through
h⁴. The task score is the mean over the graded plants. A plant whose schedule or workbook cannot be parsed
scores 0.

Two things the library will not settle for you, and which the design basis must therefore record: the
outdoor wet-bulb basis, which two adopted documents state differently for two different calculations, and
the evaporation formulation, of which the adopted documents carry two. Either evaporation formulation may
be used for the water balance and the allocation checks; the grader scores the one you declare, so declare
it and use it consistently. The life-cycle cost analysis criteria say which quantities the economic
analysis prices.

Work from the documents. Where they leave something to the engineer, decide it and record it in the
design basis.

Two properties of the library's files, stated so that a text-only reader is not disadvantaged: some
tables in the vendor PDFs extract from the text layer with their column headers broken across lines,
while each data row stays intact and in column order; and the equations of the water treatment manual
are set in a mathematical bold typeface that extracts as Unicode mathematical characters, often with
each character doubled. The numbers are still there in that form, and some of them are also stated in
the surrounding prose, but not all.

documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the

DC-02 Mechanical Design Criteria Memorandum - Condenser Water Heat Rejection
Papago Federal Center, Phoenix, Arizona | Revision 3, 14 August 2026 | Sandoval Klee Mechanical Engineers, PC
This memorandum supersedes DC-02 Revision 2 in its entirety. Revision 3 adds the life-cycle cost objective (paragraph 4, EC-01) and the LifeCycleCost sheet of Appendix A.2.
[Heading 1] 1. Scope
This memorandum states the criteria, conventions and deliverable requirements for the replacement of the condenser water heat rejection plants serving the Courthouse Central Utility Plant (CUP), the Data Annex (ANNEX) and the Laboratory Wing (LAB). The chillers, the condenser water pumps' hydraulic circuits and the electrical distribution are existing or already procured and are not in the scope of this design.
[Heading 1] 2. Adopted criteria
<<TABLE>>
Document | Status on this project

The circulating water chemistry of this project - the cycles of concentration, the dissolved solids, the scaling indices and their limits - is governed by this manual and by the treatment memorandum WT-01, not by the agency facilities standard. In particular, PBS-P100 paragraph 5.3.5.3 caps the total dissolved solids of an open condenser water system at 1,500 ppm; the reclaimed supply of this project already exceeds that figure before any concentration, so no cycles of concentration could meet it, and it does not govern this reclaimed-water supply. The alkalinity range of the same P100 paragraph is met by the acid feed WT-01 specifies.
UFC 3-230-13, Industrial Water Treatment (2023) | SUPERSEDED by UFM 3-230-13. Retained in the project library for reference only. Do not cite it as authority.
UFC 3-400-02, Engineering Weather Data (2018, Change 2) | CANCELLED. The copy in the project library is the cancelled edition: its file name records it, and its pages carry a CANCELLED watermark that is drawn letter by letter and does not survive text extraction. Retained for reference only; do not cite it as authority. The climatic basis for this project is paragraph 5.2 below.
10 CFR Part 431 Subpart B, Electric Motors | Applies to the motors furnished with the equipment.
10 CFR Part 436 Subpart A, Methodology and Procedures for Life Cycle Cost Analyses | Adopted. Governs the selection of each plant among the compliant designs (life-cycle net savings). EC-01 states how it is applied on this project.
EC-01 Life-Cycle Cost Analysis Criteria (Revision 0) | Adopted. The base date, schedule, basic design, cost data and study period of the life-cycle cost analysis.
Annual Supplement to NIST Handbook 135, 2025 edition - data tables (NIST data release doi:10.18434/mds2-3848, economics/) | Adopted as the source of the discount rate and the present-value factors (10 CFR 436.14).
NIST IR 85-3273-39, Annual Supplement to NIST Handbook 135, 2024 edition | SUPERSEDED by the 2025 edition. Its text is retained for the explanation of the tables and the method; none of its rates, factors or example numbers may be used.
EnergyPlus reference implementation source and performance data sets (vendor_data/) | Adopted as the simulation basis: the variable speed tower approach correlation and its validity limits, the tower fan power and water use treatment, the electric chiller capacity and input ratio model, and the psychrometric property relations. The two performance data set files and the three source files govern, together with the coefficient objects they are evaluated with. The shipped source is CondenserLoopTowers.cc, ChillerElectricEIR.cc, Psychrometrics.cc with its header Psychrometrics.hh (which carries the bodies of the inline property helpers the tower water-use routine calls) and CurveManager.cc (which shows that a performance curve clamps its inputs to the limits the curve object states).
<<END TABLE>>
[Heading 1] 3. Plants and served loads
<<TABLE>>
Plant | Building | Chillers | Design block load (tons) | Design chilled water supply (deg F) | Motor control center
CUP | Courthouse Central Utility Plant | 2 x CH-A (see M-601) | 820.0 | 44.0 | MCC-R1
ANNEX | Data Annex Condenser Water Plant | 2 x CH-B (see M-601) | 880.0 | 44.0 | MCC-R2
LAB | Laboratory Wing Condenser Water Plant | 3 x CH-C (see M-601) | 1070.0 | 45.0 | MCC-R3
<<END TABLE>>
Block cooling loads as a function of outdoor dry-bulb temperature are scheduled on M-603. Chiller performance data and condenser water limits are on M-601 and submittal VD-03.
[Heading 1] 4. Objective
Each plant must be designed for the HIGHEST LIFE-CYCLE NET SAVINGS, relative to the basic design, consistent with every requirement of the adopted criteria and of this memorandum, with the life-cycle cost analysis performed as EC-01 directs under 10 CFR Part 436 Subpart A. It is not the design with the lowest energy, nor the one with the lowest first cost, unless the analysis makes it so.
Annual plant electrical energy - the energy quantity the analysis prices - is the sum over the scenario bins of paragraph 5.3 of the bin hours multiplied by the coincident electrical demand of the chillers, the tower fans and the condenser water pumps of that plant.
[Heading 1] 5. Climatic and property basis
[Heading 2] 5.1 Governing station
The climatic basis is the National Centers for Environmental Information Local Climatological Data record of the airport station serving the site, for the three complete calendar years in the project library. That record is the period of record (POR) for every percentile in this memorandum. Only observations whose report type is FM-15 or FM-16 are counted; the daily and monthly summary rows of the record are not observations. Records for any other station in the library are not part of the POR.
[Heading 2] 5.2 Design outdoor conditions
A percentile design value is the value that was exceeded that percentage of the observations over the entire POR, taken as a single annual population (not a seasonal one). The design outdoor wet-bulb temperature for the heat rejection equipment is the 1.0 percent annual wet-bulb temperature so computed, adjusted as the adopted HVAC criteria require for open cooling towers. The failure-case calculation of paragraph 6.3 uses the wet-bulb basis that the adopted agency facilities standard prescribes for evaporative machines, adjusted the same way. Do not take design values from the cancelled weather-data criteria document.
[Heading 2] 5.3 Scenario bins
Annual performance is evaluated on scenario bins formed from the POR observations: bin each observation by wet-bulb temperature in 2 deg F bins and by dry-bulb temperature in 5 deg F bins, take the bin condition as the bin mid-points, and scale the bin counts so that the bins total 8760 hours per year. The block load of a bin is the M-603 load at the bin dry-bulb temperature. Where a bin's dry-bulb mid-point would fall below its wet-bulb mid-point, the dry-bulb temperature is taken equal to the wet-bulb mid-point. The bin edges fall at whole multiples of the bin width measured from zero deg F: an observation belongs to the bin whose lower edge is the largest such multiple that does not exceed it, the lower edge belonging to the bin and the upper edge to the next one, so that a bin's mid-point is its lower edge plus half the bin width.
[Heading 2] 5.4 Freeze protection
A basin heater and heat-traced makeup piping are required only where the 99.6 percent annual dry-bulb temperature computed from the POR is at or below 32 deg F. The design basis must state the computed 99.6 percent dry-bulb temperature and the determination that follows from it.
[Heading 2] 5.5 Property basis
Moist air properties are those of the psychrometric routines of the reference implementation in the project library (saturation pressure over water, humidity ratio from dry- and wet-bulb, moist air enthalpy and density, and saturation temperature from enthalpy). The barometric pressure is the mean station pressure of the governing POR, not a sea-level or a standard-atmosphere value. Water is taken at 8.33 lb/gal and 1.0 BTU/lb-deg F, so that heat rejection in BTU/h is 500 times the flow in gpm times the range in deg F.
[Heading 1] 6. Plant configuration and operating conventions
[Heading 2] 6.1 Cells and controls
All cells of a plant are of one model and one size and carry identical fan, motor, drift eliminator and material selections. Every tower fan motor is driven by a variable frequency drive. The number of cells must be a whole multiple of the number of chillers served.
[Heading 2] 6.2 Condenser water flow
Each chiller has a dedicated constant-speed condenser water pump. The scheduled design flow is the flow with every chiller running; the flow with n chillers running is n/N of it. The per-chiller flow must lie inside the condenser flow limits of submittal VD-03 and the per-cell flow inside the limits of submittal VD-01.
[Heading 2] 6.3 Redundancy
The plant must meet its design block load with the largest single cell out of service, at the failure-case wet-bulb basis of paragraph 5.2, with the remaining cells at full fan speed, and at an entering condenser water temperature no warmer than the machines' published maximum (submittal VD-03). This is the cooling robustness performance tier the agency facilities standard requires.
With a cell out of service the design condenser water flow is unchanged - every chiller is still running on its dedicated constant-speed pump (paragraph 6.2) - and it is carried by the cells that remain in service. The flow through each remaining cell in that state must lie inside the per-cell flow limits of submittal VD-01 and inside the water flow rate ratio limits of the performance object (paragraph 6.8). A plant whose remaining cells would have to pass more than that does not meet this requirement, whatever temperature a calculation extrapolated beyond those limits might predict: a cell above its rated distribution capacity and outside the validity envelope of its performance model has no substantiated capability. The clamping described in the second part of paragraph 6.8 applies to the inlet wet-bulb temperature only; it does not apply to the water flow rate ratio, in this case or any other.
[Heading 2] 6.4 Condenser water pump power
Condenser water pump total head is taken as a fixed static lift plus a friction component that varies with the square of the flow ratio:
    H = H_static + (H_pipe + H_condenser) x (Q / Q_ref)^2        [ft of water]
    Pump shaft power = Q x H / (3960 x eta_pump)                 [hp, Q in gpm]
    Pump electrical input = shaft power x 0.7457 / eta_motor     [kW]
where Q is the flow through one pump. The per-plant constants are:
<<TABLE>>
Plant | Q_ref (gpm) | H_static (ft) | H_pipe at Q_ref (ft) | H_condenser at Q_ref (ft) | eta_pump | eta_motor
CUP | 1500.0 | 24.0 | 26.0 | 21.0 | 0.78 | 0.945
ANNEX | 1500.0 | 21.0 | 23.0 | 21.0 | 0.77 | 0.945
LAB | 1065.0 | 27.0 | 29.0 | 19.0 | 0.77 | 0.945
<<END TABLE>>
[Heading 2] 6.5 Chiller staging
Chillers stage on in order: the smallest number of machines whose available capacity at the operating leaving chilled water and entering condenser water temperatures meets the block load runs, and the load is divided equally between them.
Available capacity here is the capacity the adopted performance data set makes available at those temperatures: the machine's reference capacity multiplied by its capacity-as-a-function-of-temperature curve evaluated at the operating point, and nothing else. The maximum part load ratio is not part of available capacity. It is a separate published limit - the ceiling on the load a machine that is already running may be given - and it is not applied to the capacity that decides how many machines run.
[Heading 2] 6.6 Cell staging
Condenser water is distributed to every installed cell unless the resulting per-cell flow would fall below the effective minimum, which is the larger of the submittal's minimum per-cell flow and the flow at which the performance object's minimum water flow rate ratio is reached. Cells are then isolated one at a time until the per-cell flow is at or above the effective minimum. Tower fans of the cells in service modulate together.
[Heading 2] 6.7 Condenser water supply temperature control
The condenser water supply temperature setpoint is scheduled as a wet-bulb-following reset: the setpoint is the larger of a scheduled floor and the outdoor wet-bulb temperature plus a scheduled offset, and is in no case below the minimum entering condenser water temperature the chillers are rated for. The fans modulate to the setpoint exactly as the reference implementation models a variable speed tower: full speed when the setpoint cannot be met, free convection when the fans are not needed, minimum speed with cycling below that. A condenser water bypass valve holds the setpoint when the tower would otherwise overcool, so the supply temperature never falls below the setpoint.
[Heading 2] 6.8 Validity of the performance correlation
A cell may not be operated at a water flow rate ratio outside the limits stated in the performance object, because the implementation clamps the ratio there and the capability would not be substantiated. The range, approach and liquid-to-gas ratio limits of the same object apply at every scenario. A design that operates outside them is not accepted.
The inlet air wet-bulb temperature is treated differently, and deliberately. The reference implementation clamps it to the object's stated range before evaluating the correlation, so an outdoor wet bulb at or above the object's maximum is evaluated AT that maximum and is never extrapolated. The design outdoor wet bulb of paragraph 5.2 lands on that maximum at this site. That is not an error and no work-around is required: it is what the adopted simulation basis does, and the wet-bulb limit is therefore not one of the envelope limits this paragraph tests.
[Heading 2] 6.9 Design point
At the design outdoor wet bulb of paragraph 5.2 and the design block load, with every chiller running at the scheduled design flow and the cells in service at full fan speed, the cells must deliver condenser water no warmer than the scheduled design supply temperature (CWSDESIGN), and the chillers must carry the design block load at that entering condenser water temperature. The validity limits of paragraph 6.8 - the water flow rate ratio limits, and the range, approach and liquid-to-gas ratio limits - apply at this design point as they do at every scenario. A schedule may be conservative: a CWSDESIGN warmer than the selected cells actually need is acceptable.
[Heading 2] 6.10 Peak coincident demand
The peak coincident electrical demand of a plant is the largest total electrical demand of the chillers, the tower fans and the condenser water pumps operating together, taken over the scenario bins of paragraph 5.3 and over nothing else. It is a maximum over those bins, not a design-day figure: neither the design point of paragraph 6.9 nor the redundancy case of paragraph 6.3 is a scenario bin - they are sizing conditions - and neither enters this maximum. Basin heaters, controls and lighting are not part of it. This is the quantity the motor control centre's spare capacity limits and the quantity the calculation workbook reports.
[Heading 1] 7. Water
The water balance, the cycles of concentration and the treatment programme are governed by the adopted water treatment manual and by the reclaimed water correspondence and treatment memorandum in the project library.
Two evaporation formulations are adopted for this project, and they are these two, named so that the choice is between two fully specified methods:
  SATURATED-EXIT - the moist-air method of the reference implementation's tower water-use routine: the outlet air is saturated at the inlet enthalpy plus the water-side heat transfer divided by the air mass flow, and the evaporated mass is the air mass flow times the rise in specific humidity, converted to a volume with the density of water. As the routine computes them, the inlet enthalpy is that of saturated air at the inlet wet-bulb temperature, and the water density is taken at the mean of the inlet dry-bulb and the saturated outlet air temperatures, not below 4 deg C. The routine reads that density from fluid property tables that are not part of the shipped source; on this project it is taken as rho = 1000 x (1 - (T + 288.9414) / (508929.2 x (T + 68.12963)) x (T - 3.9863)^2) kg/m3, T in deg C. Every other quantity the method needs is in the shipped source and its header.
  LOSS-FACTOR - the rule of thumb of the adopted water treatment manual's cooling tower chapter, with the constant and the temperature basis that chapter states and its own worked example confirms. It is NOT the reference implementation's user-factor path: that path reads a loss factor from an input field this project does not set, and the input dictionary that would supply a default for it is not part of the adopted basis.
Either may be used. The design basis must state which one was used, and the water balance of the submitted workbook must be computed consistently with the stated choice throughout.
[Heading 1] 8. Deliverable
For each plant P in {CUP, ANNEX, LAB} deliver CT_SCHEDULE_P.dxf and CT_CALC_P.xlsx, and once for the package constraint_register.csv and design_basis.md. Appendix A fixes the formats.
[Heading 1] 9. Design basis content
The design basis must state, for each plant, the governing constraint on the design in the form:
    GOVERNING CONSTRAINT <plant>: <name> (relative margin <value>)
where <name> is exactly one of the following six, and is the one with the smallest relative margin at the submitted design, and <value> is that relative margin:
<<TABLE>>
Name | Relative margin at the submitted design
water allocation | (annual allocation - annual makeup) / annual allocation
electrical capacity | (spare capacity - peak coincident demand) / spare capacity
roof area | (equipment zone area - area occupied by the cell supports and their required clearances) / equipment zone area
structural capacity | min over the cells of (allowable superimposed load - operating weight per unit support area) / allowable superimposed load
condenser flow limit | min over the EQUIPMENT flow limits of this project of (limit - scheduled value) / limit, taken on whichever side binds. The equipment flow limits meant here are exactly four: the minimum and maximum condenser water flow per machine of submittal VD-03, and the minimum and maximum water flow per cell of submittal VD-01. The water flow rate ratio limits of the performance object are a validity requirement of paragraph 6.8 and are NOT a margin candidate here: a design is either inside them or it is not a valid design at all
tower capability | (scheduled design approach - recomputed design approach) / scheduled design approach
<<END TABLE>>
The six names above are the only admissible values of <name>. Where two of them are within 0.004 of each other at the submitted design, either may be stated.
The margins are judged against the quantities the calculation workbook reports, not against a figure to a precision the workbook cannot carry. A relative margin is a small difference divided by a limit, so it is far more sensitive than the quantity it is computed from: near a limit, a 1 percent difference in peak demand can move the margin by more than half its value. The stated margin is therefore accepted when it agrees, within 0.004, with the margin computed from the workbook's own reported peak coincident demand, annual makeup and design supply temperature - provided each of those reported quantities is itself within the tolerance the calculation checks apply to it (peak demand and annual makeup within 10 percent of the recomputed values, supply temperature within the larger of 0.8 deg F and 10 percent of the approach). A reported quantity outside its tolerance is replaced by the recomputed value. The name is accepted when it is the smallest of the six margins so computed, with the same 0.004 tie. The roof area, structural and condenser flow margins depend only on published data and the schedule, so they are computed exactly.
The design basis must also state which weather basis was applied and the clause that requires it, and which evaporation formulation was used.
[Heading 2] 9.1 Documented conflicts
The project library contains documents that do not agree with one another. Paragraph 2 resolves several of those disagreements directly. The design basis must record how each of the three conflicts below was resolved, one line each, in the form below; these are the three this memorandum requires a line for, not a complete list of every place the library's documents differ:
    CONFLICT <n>: ADOPTED <document> <clause> | SET ASIDE <document> <clause>
where <document> is the designation the document gives itself and <clause> is the paragraph, table or revision within it. The three conflicts, in this order:
<<TABLE>>
n | The conflict to resolve
1 | The outdoor design condition on which COOLING TOWER SELECTION is based. The adopted agency facilities standard names one basis for tower selection in its HVAC design criteria paragraph; the adopted HVAC criteria document and paragraph 5.2 of this memorandum name a different one. Paragraph 2 of this memorandum allocates the subject matter.
2 | The edition of the industrial water treatment criteria that governs the treatment programme, the water balance and the scaling indices.
3 | The revision of the roof mechanical plan that fixes the equipment zone and the outdoor air intake positions.
<<END TABLE>>
A conflict is resolved by naming the document and clause that governs and the document and clause that does not. Both sides must be named. The grader reads these lines; it does not read prose around them.
[Heading 1] Appendix A - Deliverable formats
[Heading 2] A.1 CT_SCHEDULE_P.dxf
Plan units are feet, in the coordinates of M-401. Three layers are read:
  M-CTWR-SCHD - one TEXT or MTEXT entity per scheduled field, written as '<TAG> <KEY> <VALUE>'. TAG is CT-1 ... CT-n for the cell rows and PLANT for the plant rows. Values are plain numbers or the listed keywords; units are not written into the value.
<<TABLE>>
Row | Keys
Each cell CT-n | MODEL, GPM, FANHP, MOTOREFF, MOTORPOLES, MOTORENCL, ELIMINATOR, DRIFT, MATERIAL, OPWEIGHT, SOUNDLW
PLANT | CELLS, GPMTOTAL, WBDESIGN, CWSDESIGN, RANGEDESIGN, APPROACHDESIGN, CWSMIN, CWSOFFSET, COC, BASINCLR, EVAPMETHOD, BASINHEATER, BLOWDOWNCTRL, EQUALIZING
<<END TABLE>>
MOTOREFF is the nominal full-load efficiency in percent. DRIFT is the drift rate in percent of design water flow. COC is the cycles of concentration the plant is controlled to. BASINCLR is the clear dimension in feet between the top of the roof and the underside of the tower basin. EVAPMETHOD is SATURATED-EXIT or LOSS-FACTOR. BASINHEATER, BLOWDOWNCTRL and EQUALIZING are YES or NO.
  GPM is the flow through one cell with every installed cell in service, that is GPMTOTAL divided by CELLS. Where the staging rule of paragraph 6.6 leaves a cell out of service at some operating point, the scheduled figure does not change; the flow actually in each cell at each scenario belongs in the off-design table.
  M-CTWR-PLAN - one closed LWPOLYLINE per cell, the rectangular plan outline of that cell's support frame, in the plan coordinates of M-401, which places the three plants on one sheet each on its own origin. One polyline per installed cell, no more and no fewer.
  G-TBLK - the title block, including the sheet revision.
[Heading 2] A.2 CT_CALC_P.xlsx
Five sheets. DesignPoint, WaterBalance, Energy and LifeCycleCost are two-column key/value sheets with the key in column A and the value in column B. OffDesign is a table with a header row.
<<TABLE>>
Sheet | Required keys or columns
DesignPoint | DesignWetBulb_F, DesignLoad_tons, HeatRejection_BTUH, CWFlow_gpm, Range_F, Approach_F, CWS_F, CWR_F, WaterFlowRatio, CellsInService, RedundancyWetBulb_F, RedundancyCapacity_tons, DryBulb996_F
OffDesign | WetBulb_F, DryBulb_F, Hours, Load_tons, ChillersOn, CellsOn, CWFlow_gpm, AirFlowRatio, FanPLR, Range_F, CWS_F, CWR_F, ChillerkW, FankW, PumpkW, TotalkW, Makeup_gpm - one row per scenario bin of paragraph 5.3
WaterBalance | EvaporationMethod, AnnualEvaporation_kgal, AnnualDrift_kgal, AnnualBlowdown_kgal, AnnualMakeup_kgal, PeakDayMakeup_gal, CyclesOfConcentration, MaxAllowableCOC, ScalingIndexAtCWR
Energy | AnnualChillerEnergy_kWh, AnnualFanEnergy_kWh, AnnualPumpEnergy_kWh, AnnualPlantEnergy_kWh, PeakCoincidentDemand_kW, MCCSpareCapacity_kW
LifeCycleCost | DiscountRate, StudyPeriod_yr, ConstructionPeriod_yr, UPVStarElectricity, UPVStarWater, UPVNonFuel, Investment_USD, AnnualEnergyCost_USD, AnnualWaterCost_USD, AnnualOMCost_USD, PVEnergy_USD, PVWater_USD, PVOM_USD, PVReplacement_USD, PVSalvage_USD, LCC_USD, BasicDesignLCC_USD, NetSavings_USD
<<END TABLE>>
Values are numbers, not text with units, and no cell may be left blank or carry a placeholder.
RedundancyCapacity_tons is the total cooling capacity the plant's chillers can deliver with the largest tower cell out of service, evaluated at the failure-case wet bulb of paragraph 6.3 with the remaining cells at full fan speed, at the entering condenser water temperature those remaining cells actually produce at that wet bulb and at the scheduled condenser water flow. It is the capacity available at that operating point, not the capacity available at the machine's rated maximum entering condenser water temperature, and not the reference capacity of the performance data set. It is available capacity in the sense of paragraph 6.5, so the maximum part load ratio is not applied to it. RedundancyWetBulb_F is the wet bulb it is evaluated at.
LifeCycleCost: DiscountRate is the real discount rate as a fraction or in percent. StudyPeriod_yr and ConstructionPeriod_yr are in years from the base date. UPVStarElectricity, UPVStarWater and UPVNonFuel are the present-value factors the analysis multiplies the base-year annual electricity cost, water and sewer cost, and non-fuel operation and maintenance cost by, to give their present values at the base date over the period in which they accrue. AnnualEnergyCost_USD (energy and demand charges), AnnualWaterCost_USD (reclaimed water and sewer) and AnnualOMCost_USD (treatment and routine maintenance) are base-year amounts; PVEnergy_USD, PVWater_USD and PVOM_USD their present values; PVReplacement_USD and PVSalvage_USD the present values of replacements and of the salvage value (a positive number, subtracted in LCC_USD); LCC_USD the life-cycle cost of the design as scheduled, BasicDesignLCC_USD that of the EC-01 basic design of the same plant, and NetSavings_USD their difference. All dollar amounts are constant base-date dollars.
FanPLR is the fan part load ratio of the cells in service at that scenario bin, as the reference implementation of paragraph 6.7 reports it for a variable speed tower: 1.0 where the fans run, whether at full speed or modulating to the setpoint; 0.0 where the fans are off; and the cycling ratio where the cells cycle at the minimum fan speed. The speed itself is reported separately as AirFlowRatio.
The DesignPoint sheet reports the performance the SELECTED equipment achieves at the design point - the range, approach, supply and return temperatures and water flow rate ratio that follow from the scheduled model, cell count and flow - and not the scheduled target. Where a design is scheduled conservatively, so that CWSDESIGN is warmer than the cells actually need, the schedule carries the conservative number and this sheet carries the achieved one.

=================== EC-01_Life_Cycle_Cost_Analysis_Criteria
EC-01 Life-Cycle Cost Analysis Criteria - Condenser Water Heat Rejection Replacement
Papago Federal Center, Phoenix, Arizona | Revision 0, 14 August 2026 | Sandoval Klee Mechanical Engineers, PC for the General Services Administration
[Heading 1] 1. Governing rule
The tower selection for each plant is an energy and water conservation investment in a Federal building and is selected under the Federal life-cycle cost methodology of 10 CFR Part 436, Subpart A (copy in standards/). The alternative tower selections for a plant are mutually exclusive alternatives for one building energy system. Each plant is designed for the HIGHEST NET SAVINGS, in the sense of 10 CFR 436.18(e) and 436.20, relative to the basic design of paragraph 5, among the designs that meet every requirement of the adopted criteria and of DC-02. Net savings of a design = life-cycle cost of the basic design - life-cycle cost of the design.
[Heading 1] 2. Base date and analysis basis
The base date of the analysis is 1 October 2025, the first day of the FY2026 base year. The analysis is a constant-dollar analysis at base-date prices with the real discount rate (10 CFR 436.14(a)), using the end-of-year conventions of the tables it takes its factors from.
[Heading 1] 3. Schedule
The design and construction period is 1 year from the base date; beneficial occupancy of the replaced plants is 1 October 2026. Investment costs are taken as a lump sum at the base date (10 CFR 436.14(f)). Energy, water and operation and maintenance costs begin to accrue at beneficial occupancy, not at the base date (436.14(g)); their present values are found as 10 CFR 436.16(c), 436.17(b) and 436.17(d) direct for costs that begin to accrue after the base date.
[Heading 1] 4. Discount rate, energy escalation and present-value factors
The discount rate, the projected escalation of energy prices and the present-value factors are those of the Annual Supplement to NIST Handbook 135 in force at the base date, as 10 CFR 436.14(a) and (b) require: the 2025 edition. Its data tables - NIST data release doi:10.18434/mds2-3848 - are in economics/ and govern every rate and factor. The project library holds the text of the 2024 edition (NIST IR 85-3273-39) for its explanation of the tables and the method; the tables and the method are organised the same way in both editions, but every rate, factor and worked-example number printed in the 2024 edition is SUPERSEDED by the 2025 data release and must not be used.
Energy conservation projects use the DOE (FEMP) factors and discount rate, not the OMB Circular A-94 factors, which apply to other Federal investments. The site is in Arizona; the electricity is purchased under the commercial general service schedule of letter UT-01. Take the factors for that location, that sector and that fuel. Use the tables as they are printed, without shifting their base year: the year counts of the tables are years from the base date of this analysis.
[Heading 1] 5. Basic design
The basic design of 10 CFR 436.20 for each plant is the replacement of the existing cells in kind, operated as the existing plants are operated:

The basic design is evaluated with the same simulation basis, scenario bins, staging and control conventions as a proposed design (DC-02) and priced exactly as a proposed design is priced (paragraph 6). It is a reference for net savings only; it is not required to meet the criteria and it is not a candidate selection.
[Heading 1] 6. Cost data

Electricity | UT-01 energy charge and demand charge | Annual energy = annual plant electrical energy of DC-02 paragraph 4; because of the UT-01 ratchet the plant adds its peak coincident demand of DC-02 paragraph 6.10 to the billing demand of every month (twelve months a year). [Heading 1] 7. Study period, replacement and salvage
The study period is set by 10 CFR 436.14(d)(2)(i) for mutually exclusive alternatives, the alternatives being the tower selections VD-01 and VD-05 offer that the adopted criteria admit, with their design service lives from the VD-05 ServiceLife sheet. The study period runs from the base date: the design and construction period of paragraph 3 followed by the service period. A cell placed in service at beneficial occupancy with a service life shorter than the service period is replaced when its life expires, at the installed price of one cell as VD-05 states it; the plant controls item is not replaced. Salvage value at the end of the study period is straight-line: the replacement cost multiplied by the unexpired fraction of the service life of the equipment then in service. Replacement and salvage are single amounts discounted from the year in which they occur.

Papago Federal Center, Condenser Water Heat Rejection Replacement | Issued for construction documents, 14 August 2026
[Heading 1] PART 1 - GENERAL
[Heading 2] 1.1 Summary
Factory assembled, induced draught, counterflow, film fill, field erected on structural steel dunnage, open evaporative cooling tower cells with variable frequency driven fans, for condenser water service.
[Heading 2] 1.2 Performance certification
Thermal performance of each cell must be certified under CTI Standard STD-201 for the scheduled duty. Where a model is not certified, a field acceptance test under CTI ATC-105 at the contractor's expense is required.
[Heading 1] PART 2 - PRODUCTS
[Heading 2] 2.1 Acceptable manufacturers
Cells of the CTX Series C range in submittal VD-01, or an approved equal of the same certified capability, plan dimensions and operating weight.
[Heading 2] 2.2 Materials
Water contact surfaces, including the cold water basin, the casing below the operating water line, the distribution basin and all fasteners in the water stream, must comply with the materials requirement of the agency facilities standard for cooling towers. Confirm the selected material option against that requirement; the manufacturer offers options that do not comply. Structural steel dunnage is hot-dip galvanised after fabrication; dunnage is not a water contact surface.
[Heading 2] 2.3 Drift eliminators
Cellular PVC drift eliminators, removable in sections. The certified drift rate of the selected eliminator must not exceed 0.002 percent of the design circulating water flow rate at design air flow. Eliminator classes and their certified drift rates are in submittal VD-04. The drift rate used in the water balance must be the certified rate of the eliminator actually selected.
[Heading 2] 2.4 Basin and blowdown
Cold water basin with a sloped sump, sweeper piping, an overflow, a drain, a make-up connection with an electrically actuated valve and an air gap, and an electrically actuated automatic blowdown valve controlled from a conductivity controller. Provide connections and mounting for the chemical metering pumps of the water treatment programme. A basin heater and heat traced make-up piping are provided only where the design criteria memorandum requires them.
[Heading 2] 2.5 Fans and drives
Axial propeller fans on right angle gear reducers, with a variable frequency drive on each fan motor. Fan motors are totally enclosed fan cooled, squirrel cage induction, NEMA Design B, suitable for inverter duty, and must comply with the federal energy conservation standard for the applicable motor category. The fan must not draw more than the motor nameplate horsepower at any operating point in the scheduled sequence; the gear reducer service factor is not available as fan power.
[Heading 2] 2.6 Sound
The A-weighted sound power level of each cell at full fan speed must not exceed 102 dB re 1 pW. Sound power levels of the offered cells are in submittal VD-01.
[Heading 2] 2.7 Equalising and isolation
Where more than one cell is installed, provide equalising lines between the cold water basins and automatic isolation valves on the supply to each cell, so that any cell may be taken out of service with its chiller running, as the agency facilities standard requires.
[Heading 1] PART 3 - EXECUTION
[Heading 2] 3.1 Installation
Set cells on structural steel dunnage on the roof framing zones indicated on S-401, within the equipment zone indicated on M-401 Revision C. Maintain the air inlet clearances of submittal VD-01 on every air inlet face and between adjacent cells, and the clearance between the top of the roof and the underside of the basin that the agency facilities standard requires.

EXCERPT. This section covers the CLOSED hydronic systems of the project. The condenser water (open evaporative) treatment programme is specified in the water treatment memorandum WT-01 and is not covered by this section.

Provide a nitrite-molybdate closed system inhibitor at 800 to 1,200 ppm as nitrite, with a tolyltriazole yellow metal inhibitor at 5 to 10 ppm. Maintain closed system pH between 8.5 and 10.5. Closed systems do not concentrate and have no cycles of concentration, no blowdown and no evaporative makeup.
[Heading 1] 2.2 Glycol
Where freeze protection is required, use inhibited propylene glycol at 30 percent by volume, with a freeze point of -13 deg F and a burst point of -60 deg F. Ethylene glycol is prohibited. Correct the pump head and the heat transfer capacity for the glycol properties at the operating temperature: at 30 percent propylene glycol the specific heat is 0.90 and the specific gravity is 1.02 at 100 deg F, so the flow required for a given duty and range increases by approximately 9 percent.
[Heading 1] 2.3 Glycol feed
Provide a 55 gallon glycol feed unit with a pressure switch, a low level alarm and a backflow preventer for each closed system requiring glycol.
[Heading 1] 2.4 Testing
Test closed system inhibitor concentration monthly for the first six months and quarterly thereafter.

=================== WT-01_Water_Treatment_Program_Memo
WT-01 Condenser Water Treatment Programme Memorandum
Papago Federal Center | Revision 1, 14 August 2026 | Prepared by Verde Basin Water Technologies, Inc. for the Engineer of Record
[Heading 1] 1. Supply
Condenser water makeup for all three plants is Class A+ reclaimed water delivered by the municipal purveyor from the reclamation facility, at the allocation and discharge limits of letter PW-LTR-014. The supply is the same for the three plants.
[Heading 1] 2. Analysis of record
The analysis of record for the supply is the most recent COMPLETE analysis in the Water Quality Portal result set in the project library, where a complete analysis is one that reports dissolved calcium, dissolved alkalinity, total dissolved solids in mg/L, dissolved sulfate and dissolved silica from the same sampling date. Field-parameter-only visits are not complete analyses. Earlier complete analyses in the same result set are superseded by the most recent one and must not be used for the selection.
Calcium is reported in the result set as mg/L as Ca. Calcium hardness as CaCO3 is the reported dissolved calcium multiplied by 2.497. The 'Hardness, Ca, Mg' result is total hardness and includes magnesium; it is not calcium hardness and must not be used in the indices. Where a determinand is reported both as dissolved and as recoverable, the dissolved result is used. Results reported in tons per acre-foot or tons per day are loading figures, not concentrations. Where total dissolved solids is reported in mg/L both as measured residue on evaporation and as a value computed from the constituents, the measured residue on evaporation is the value of record.
[Heading 1] 3. Programme
The programme is a phosphonate and polymer stabilised alkaline programme with sulphuric acid feed. The acid feed holds the circulating M-alkalinity at 120 ppm as CaCO3 at all cycles of concentration; alkalinity therefore does not cycle up. Total dissolved solids and calcium hardness cycle up in proportion to the cycles of concentration. A conductivity controller with an automatic blowdown valve and metering pumps for the inhibitor and the biocide are required at every plant, as is a makeup water meter.
[Heading 1] 4. Controlling cycles of concentration
The allowable cycles of concentration are the lowest of the limits the adopted water treatment manual gives for the scale-forming salts that this programme does not address, and the limit that the calcium carbonate scaling index of the same manual permits. The inhibitor package addresses calcium carbonate AND calcium sulfate, so neither the manual's rough calcium carbonate prediction nor its calcium sulfate prediction is a controlling limit here; calcium phosphate is not applicable because the circulating orthophosphate is held below 10 ppm by the programme. Silica is not addressed by the programme and its limit applies as the manual states it.
The programme is qualified by the supplier to a computed Practical (Puckorius) Scaling Index of not less than 5.60. Below that value the dispersant cannot hold calcium carbonate in solution and the programme is not warranted. The index is evaluated at the hottest waterside temperature of the system, which for these plants is the condenser water return temperature at the design point - the return temperature the selected cells actually produce there (the CWR the calculation workbook's design point sheet reports), not a scheduled figure - and at the circulating concentrations that the selected cycles of concentration produce.
[Heading 2] 4.1 Evaluation of the index factors
Factor B is taken from the manual's temperature table by linear interpolation. Factors A, C and D are the closed forms that the manual's tables tabulate, adopted here so that the index can be evaluated where the circulating concentration leaves the tabulated range:
    A = (log10(total dissolved solids in ppm) - 1) / 10
    C = log10(calcium hardness as CaCO3 in ppm) - 0.4
    D = log10(M-alkalinity as CaCO3 in ppm)
These reproduce the manual's tables across their whole tabulated range. The equilibrium pH is the closed form the manual's appendix gives as an alternative to its chart.
[Heading 1] 5. Other limits
Circulating pH is controlled to 8.0 to 8.6. The blowdown discharged to the sanitary sewer must not exceed the daily limit of PW-LTR-014. Legionella control follows the campus water management plan and does not change the water balance.
[Heading 1] 6. Programme cost
The programme is supplied as a full-service contract: inhibitor, dispersant, biocide, sulphuric acid, controller service and monthly testing, billed at $0.42 per 1,000 gallons of makeup water treated, at prices in effect on 1 October 2025. The contract price is adjusted for general inflation only.
=================== RFI-031_Response_Weather_Basis_and_Setpoints
RFI-031 Response - Weather Basis, Redundancy Basis and Condenser Water Setpoint Policy
Papago Federal Center | Response issued 21 August 2026 | Engineer of Record: Sandoval Klee Mechanical Engineers, PC
[Heading 1] Question 1
The adopted HVAC criteria and the adopted agency facilities standard give different outdoor wet-bulb bases for evaporative machines. Which governs the tower selection, and which governs the failure-case calculation?
[Heading 2] Response 1
Both govern, for different calculations, and neither is waived. Size the cells - the design point, the scheduled design approach and the redundancy capacity check - on the basis the HVAC criteria give for open cooling towers and wet closed-circuit cooling towers, which is the 1.0 percent annual wet-bulb temperature with the adder that clause states. Perform the cooling robustness (largest machine out of service) calculation on the evaporation design wet-bulb basis the agency facilities standard names in its cooling robustness requirement, with the same adder applied. Compute both percentiles from the station period of record identified in DC-02 paragraph 5.1. The cancelled engineering weather data criteria document in the project library is not a source of design values on this project.
[Heading 1] Question 2
The agency standard requires variable frequency drives on the tower fans to control the condenser water supply temperature to the chillers, but does not state a reset policy. What policy should be scheduled?
[Heading 2] Response 2
Schedule a wet-bulb-following reset with two numbers: a supply temperature floor and an offset above the outdoor wet-bulb temperature. The setpoint at any hour is the larger of the two, limited below by the minimum entering condenser water temperature of the chillers served. Both numbers are the designer's to optimise and both must appear on the tower schedule. A fixed setpoint is a special case with a zero offset and is not prohibited, but it is unlikely to be the least-energy policy at this site.
[Heading 1] Question 3
The project library contains two industrial water treatment criteria documents with the same clause numbering, and two revisions of the roof mechanical plan. Which govern?
[Heading 2] Response 3
The 2026 manual governs the water treatment criteria; the 2023 criteria document it replaced is retained for reference only. Revision C of M-401 governs the roof; Revision B is superseded and its equipment zone and outdoor air intake locations must not be used. Both supersessions are recorded in DC-02 paragraph 2.
=================== RFI-034_Response_Retained_Loads_MCC
RFI-034 Response - Retained Loads on the Motor Control Centers
Papago Federal Center | Response issued 4 September 2026 | Engineer of Record: Sandoval Klee Mechanical Engineers, PC
[Heading 1] Question 1
The Laboratory Wing exhaust fan replacement, a separate contract, connects new exhaust fan motors to MCC-R3 before the heat rejection plant is commissioned. Panel schedule E-601 Revision C was prepared from the field survey of 19 February 2026. Does the spare capacity E-601 states for MCC-R3 account for these motors?
[Heading 2] Response 1
No. The three laboratory exhaust fans EF-L7, EF-L8 and EF-L9 were not connected at the time of the survey and are not in the retained existing demand of E-601. Each fan is driven by a 7.5 hp, 4 pole, totally enclosed fan cooled motor with a nominal full-load efficiency of 91.7 percent, through a variable frequency drive with an efficiency of 0.97 at rated load. The fans serve fume hood exhaust and run continuously at full speed and full nameplate load, so they operate coincident with the heat rejection plant at every hour of the year. Add their electrical input to the retained existing demand of MCC-R3 and reduce the spare capacity available to the new heat rejection plant accordingly. The bus rating and the continuous loading limit stated on E-601 are unchanged.
[Heading 1] Question 2
Are MCC-R1 and MCC-R2 affected?
[Heading 2] Response 2
No. No load has been connected to MCC-R1 or MCC-R2 since the survey, and their spare capacities are as E-601 states.

5.3.1.1 HVAC LOAD CALCULATION REQUIREMENTS 
Mechanical occupancy loads must be determined as follows: 
• 
Determine occupant density (persons/m2 or persons/ft2) from the occupancy schedule of the Project 
Program of Requirements. 
• 
In the event this information is not available, use the occupancy density values in ASHRAE 62.1.  
• 
For dining areas, auditoriums, and other high-occupancy spaces, occupancy densities must 
represent the number of seats available. 
• 
Sensible and latent loads per person must be based on the latest edition of the ASHRAE Handbook 
of Fundamentals.

CHAPTER 5 • MECHANICAL ENGINEERING 
 
Page 195

The HVAC load calculations must be performed with a computer-based program using the latest ASHRAE 
Handbook of Fundamentals Heat Balance (HB) Method, Radiant Time Series (RTS) Method, or Transfer 
Function Method (TFM), developed for the hourly analysis of heating and cooling loads in commercial 
buildings. 
The program must be capable of calculating each zone’s peak heating and cooling loads as well as the 
whole-building simultaneous peak load. The program must, at a minimum, calculate solar gains through 
fenestration; internal gains from occupants, including latent heat for cooling purposes; internal gains 
from lighting and equipment; outside air loads (sensible and latent) from ventilation and infiltration; and 
heat and moisture gains or losses through fenestration, walls, floors, and roofs. The heating load 
calculations must be done without credit for occupants and internal gains. The HVAC load calculations 
must not include additional safety factors unless specifically asked for in the applicable tenant design 
guides. 
Provide HVAC load calculations at each design phase. The HVAC load calculations report must include all 
input and output used in the heating and cooling calculation program. The report must also include zone 
peak heating and cooling loads results and whole-building simultaneous peak load, air-handling unit coil 
selections, and Psychrometric charts that show the complete cycle of all the processes in the HVAC 
system. 
5.3.1.2 ENERGY ANALYSIS 
A building energy analysis must be performed at each phase of the design to demonstrate that the 
building design meets or exceeds the energy performance goals established for the project. Energy 
software used for proof of compliance must conform to ASHRAE Standard 140. 
The compliance methodology must be in accordance with Sections 5 (except Section 5.6), 6, 7, 8, 9, and 
10 of ASHRAE 90.1. See A.7 Energy Analysis Input and Output for procedures.  
5.3.2 HVAC SYSTEMS 
All projects installing HVAC equipment must use all-electric equipment. Ensure the analysis of 
alternatives and LCCA include ground source, air source, and water source heat pump technologies. See 
Chapter 1, Electrification. 
The designer must specifically address capacity turndown with respect to minimum building loads, chiller 
tonnage/ boiler MMBtu, and pumping capacity. 
5.3.2.1 CHILLER PLANT 
Peak cooling loads must be met using equally sized chillers. The chillers must be sized to meet the peak 
cooling load. The chilled water system must be capable of turning down to 10% of peak load and 
designed to operate in a stable manner. All units must have adequate valving to isolate the offline unit 
without interruption of service. A waterside-economizer cycle must be analyzed during the design of the 
chiller plant and incorporated in the design if it improves the performance. 
In addition to meeting the minimum efficiency requirements of the latest edition of ASHRAE 90.1, air-
cooled and water-cooled electric chillers must meet the minimum Federal Energy Management Program 
(FEMP) efficiency requirements. 

--- page 197
CHAPTER 5 • MECHANICAL ENGINEERING 
 
Page 196 
 
PBS P100 2024 
New chiller equipment may only use refrigerants listed as "Acceptable" by the EPA’s Significant New 
Alternatives Policy (SNAP) Program, e.g. for centrifugal or positive displacement chillers. Refrigerants 
listed as Unacceptable may not be used in new chiller equipment at GSA projects, even where EPA's 
"unacceptable as of" date is in the future. Verify whether state and/or local jurisdictions have refrigerant 
use limitations in addition to those outlined by EPA SNAP. Refrigerants at or below 10 GWP should be 
prioritized if listed as “Acceptable” by SNAP. Only A1 Refrigerants are permitted for direct or high 
probability systems. Any refrigerant other than A1 must be contained within a machinery room 
complying with ASHRAE 15 and other applicable codes. 
New chillers may only use refrigerants that meet the Global Warming Potential (GWP) Limit and 
installation compliance date established by the EPA Technology Transitions Restrictions on the Use of 
Certain HFCs under Subsection (i) of the AIM Act. 
5.3.2.2 BOILER PLANT 
The central boiler plant within the building or on the property must be provided with equally sized 
modular boilers. The boilers must be sized to meet the peak heating load. Increasing the boiler size for 
spare or backup capacity is not permissible. The boiler system must be capable of turning down to 10% of 
peak load and design to operate in a stable manner. All units must have adequate valving to isolate the 
offline unit without interruption of service.  
In addition to meeting the minimum efficiency requirements of the latest edition of ASHRAE 90.1, boilers 
must meet the minimum Federal Energy Management Program (FEMP) efficiency requirements.  
5.3.2.3 COOLING TOWERS 
Each chiller must have its own matching cooling tower or cell, condenser, and chilled water pump. 
Multiple cooling towers must have equalizing lines and the necessary automatic control valves for 
individual chiller/cooling tower operation. The cooling tower fan(s) must be equipped with appropriately 
sized variable frequency drives to better control the condenser water supply temperature to the 
chiller(s). A minimum 4-foot clearance must be maintained between the top of the roof and underside of 
the cooling tower basin. 
5.3.2.4 WATER DISTRIBUTION SYSTEMS 
5.3.2.4.1 PRIMARY HEATING SYSTEMS 
GSA requires low-temperature hydronic heating systems, with the lowest working pressure suitable for 
the system and a maximum temperature limitation of 93.3°C (200°F).  
5.3.2.4.2 DISTRICT STEAM HEATING  
When steam is furnished to the building, it must be converted to hot water with a heat exchanger in the 
mechanical room near the entrance into the building. Steam heating is discouraged inside the building, 
other than the conversion of steam to hot water in the mechanical room. 
The designer must investigate the use of district steam condensate for preheating domestic hot water.  
5.3.2.4.3 HYDRONIC SYSTEM GLYCOL 
If glycol is used for freeze protection, it must be propylene glycol; use of ethylene glycol is prohibited.

5.3.2.4.4 PIPING SYSTEMS 
Hot water and chilled water air systems must use a four-pipe main distribution system. Dual temperature 
piping systems are not permitted.  
5.3.2.4.5 PIPING INSULATION 
Pipes operating at a temperature below ambient must be insulated with closed-cell insulation with all 
joints sealed and having a system permeance of ≤0.02 perms, such as cellular glass, or with closed-cell 
insulation covered with a continuous vapor retarder with a permeance of ≤0.02 perms. All insulation and 
vapor retarder materials must meet the appropriate ASTM material standard for that type. 
5.3.2.5 AIR DISTRIBUTION SYSTEMS 
Supply air distribution systems must be fully ducted to the spaces that are served.  
For plenum return air systems, the horizontal distance from the farthest point in the plenum to a return 
air duct must not exceed 50 feet. All transfer air openings must be sized with no more than 300 FPM air 
velocity. 
5.3.2.6 ROOF-MOUNTED EQUIPMENT 
Mechanical equipment, except for cooling towers, air-cooled chillers, Dedicated Outside Air Systems 
(DOAS), evaporative condensers, air-source heat pumps, condensing units, condensers, and exhaust fans, 
are not permitted on the roof of the building. Access to roof-mounted equipment must be by stairs or 
freight elevator; ship’s ladders are not permitted. LPOE vehicle inspection booths are exempt from this 
requirement and may have rooftop equipment provided there is an efficient and safe way to access the 
equipment for maintenance and the LPOE vehicle lanes are not blocked during the equipment 
maintenance. See Chapter 3, Roofing and Horizontal Waterproofing-Membrane System for membrane 
requirements. 
5.3.2.7 CONTROLS/BUILDING AUTOMATION SYSTEMS 
For new construction, use direct digital control (DDC) with an open BACnet communication protocol in 
accordance with ASHRAE Standard 135. 
For repair and alteration projects and new additions to existing projects, the following options are 
permitted: 1) installation of DDC with the BACnet or LonTalk protocol, 2) if existing system is primarily 
LonWorks, use of the LonTalk protocol is permitted, 3) integrating the existing system with customized 
gateways to the BACnet or LonTalk protocol. 
All specified technologies must be Native BACnet and meet GSA Smart Building requirements, see GSA 
Order ADM 7002.1 Smart Buildings. Control capabilities and the connected points must comply with GSA 
Data Normalization for Building Automation Systems document except for variable refrigerant flow (VRF) 
systems which must identify the maximum number of points meeting the requirements and obtain 
approval from Facilities Management GSA Smart Buildings personnel and GSA PB-ITS prior to BAS system 
specification. The controls must be connected to a GSA IT remediated building monitoring and control 
system and successfully pass the GSA IT Security Procedural Guide: Building Monitoring and Control 
(BMC) Systems Security Assessment Process CIO-IT Security-16-76 six step security assessment process 
prior to being specified, purchased, and installed. Standalone systems are not permitted.

Psychrometric process charts must be prepared for each air-handling unit application, characterizing full-

5.3.3.4 COOLING AND HEATING COILS 
Equipment and other obstructions in the air stream must be located sufficiently downstream of the coil 
so that it will not meet the water droplet carryover. Cooling coils must be selected at or below 2.5 m/s 
(500 fpm) face velocity. Heating coils must be selected at or below 3.8 m/s (750 fpm) face velocity.

thickness to be maintained between 0.6 –mil and 1.2- mil and with minimum salt spray resistance of

electro coating are preferable to copper fins for NOX/SOX corrosion protection from fossil fuel

Individual finned-tube cooling coils of six rows or more must not exceed 10 fins per inch.

room with all provisions made for breaching, flue stack, and combustion air. Modular systems must have 
bank controllers and grandmaster bank controllers to prevent individual modules within a bank from 
simultaneously cycling ON/OFF with another separate bank of modules.

Natural gas piping must be ASTM Sch 40. Only Sch 40 black steel pipe is acceptable. Gas piping must 
comply with Chapter 4 of the International Fuel Gas Code. Press fitting systems may be used between ½" 
to 2" where approved by code and with proper approvals and certifications but must not be used in 
concealed locations. 
STEEL PIPE FITTINGS 
For steel piping, threaded malleable iron fittings for 50mm (2in) and under, and welded Sch 40 fittings for 
pipes 64mm (2 ½in) and over are acceptable.  
Grooved fittings are acceptable for water services 110-deg C (230 deg F) and under. All grooved products 
must be of a single manufacturer. The grooving tool must be of the same manufacturer as the grooved 
components. The grooved manufacturer must provide on-site training for the contractor’s field personnel 
and must periodically visit the job site to ensure best practices in grooved joint installation are being 
followed. Grooved pipe and fittings must not be installed in concealed spaces, shafts, or above hard 
ceilings. Coordinate access for future repairs or replacements. 
Steel Press fitting systems may be used between ½" to 2" where approved by code and with proper 
approvals and certifications but must not be used in concealed locations. 
COPPER PIPE FITTINGS 
For copper piping, brazed, soldered, and press-seal (test to 2100 1050 kPa [300 150 psi]) fittings are 
acceptable. Grooved or mechanically formed T-type fittings are not acceptable. Piping must not be 
installed in concealed locations when press-seal fittings are used. 
Refrigerant piping must be Type ACR or Type K copper with brazed joints. Installation must comply with 
all requirements of ASHRAE Standard 15 Safety Standard for Refrigeration Systems and ASHRAE Standard 
34 Designation and Safety Classification of Refrigerants, refrigerant concentration limits. ASHRAE 
Standard 15 and ASHRAE Standard 34 refrigerant concentration limit calculations must be provided for 
each space containing refrigeration piping for each design phase submittal." 
Refrigerant piping must be installed in accessible areas (i.e. corridors, machine rooms, etc.) and be 
located at a ceiling height that would make the piping accessible for repair and replacement. Cooling coil 
condensate piping must be Type L copper.
